title: Writing: A Philosophical Essay on an Ethical Issue

writingModel.placeholder: State the ethical issue and your position clearly
writingModel.hint: Use "It is argued here that…" or "This essay defends the view that…"

writingModel.placeholder: Present your first argument with philosophical reasoning
writingModel.hint: Use framework language: "From a deontological perspective…" / "A consequentialist would argue…"

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the strongest objection charitably, then counter it
writingModel.hint: "One might object that… This objection has force. Nevertheless/However, it does not establish…"

writingModel.placeholder: Add a further supporting argument or qualify your claim
writingModel.hint: Use "I am not claiming X, but only Y" or "In ordinary cases X; in extreme cases Y"
"It follows that…" / "In light of the above…" / "The upshot is…"

writingTemplate.placeholder: the absolute prohibition on torture cannot be overridden by consequentialist considerations
writingTemplate.hint: State your position directly in the opening sentence

writingTemplate.placeholder: using a person as a mere means — even to save many lives — constitutes a fundamental violation of their dignity
writingTemplate.hint: Present your argument using a philosophical framework
Introduce and then counter the strongest objection
writingTemplate.placeholder: consequences must have some moral weight / it does not follow that they override all deontological constraints

writingTemplate.prefix: I am not claiming that outcomes are irrelevant, but only that
writingTemplate.placeholder: they cannot override the absolute prohibition on treating persons as mere instruments
writingTemplate.hint: "I am not claiming X, but only Y" = precise qualification

writingTemplate.prefix: In light of the above, it follows that
writingTemplate.placeholder: even granting that torture might produce good consequences, it remains morally impermissible
writingTemplate.hint: "In light of the above, it follows that…" = formal philosophical conclusion

items: This essay argues that…
I shall defend the view that…
The central claim of this essay is that…
It is argued here that neither X nor Y is fully satisfactory.
This essay takes issue with the view that…
One might object that this argument proves too much.
The strongest objection to this view is that…
This objection has genuine force. Nevertheless, it does not establish…
It is true that X. That said, Y.
Even granting this point, the main argument still holds.
I am not claiming X, but only that Y.
This is not to say that X, but rather to insist that Y.
In ordinary cases, the principle holds. In extreme dilemmas, it may require qualification.
My claim is the modest one that X, not the stronger claim that Y.
Be that as it may, the core position remains defensible.
It follows that no single ethical framework is fully adequate.
In light of the above, we may conclude that…
The upshot of this argument is that…
What this shows is that moral reasoning requires multiple frameworks.
Notwithstanding the objections, the conclusion stands: X is morally impermissible.

questions.text: "___ ___ that this argument ignores the interests of the majority." (introducing objection)
questions.hint: "One might object that…" = charitable introduction of opposing view

questions.text: "This objection has genuine force. ___, it does not establish that torture is ever permissible." (counter after concession)
"___ granting that consequences matter, it does not follow that they override all other considerations."
questions.hint: "Even granting X, Y still holds" = concede for argument's sake, then counter

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ the above, we may conclude that no single framework is adequate." (drawing conclusion)
questions.hint: "In light of the above" = formal conclusion phrase

questions.text: "___ ___ these objections, the core argument remains defensible." (formal: despite/notwithstanding)
questions.hint: "Notwithstanding X, Y" = formal version of "despite X, Y"

questions.text: "I am not claiming that outcomes are irrelevant, but only that they cannot override all constraints" uses a correct limiting structure.
questions.hint: "I am not claiming X, but only Y" = precise claim qualification

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ is that care ethics complements the other frameworks rather than replacing them." (conclusion)
questions.hint: "The upshot is that…" = the practical conclusion of the argument

questions.text: "___ is not to say that character is unimportant, but to insist that consequences also matter."
questions.hint: "This is not to say X" and "It is not to say X" are both correct
